title: Rental renovation licensing by-law and development charges shortfall
subtitle: Development charges by-law extension, affordable housing fees, BIA budgets, community grants, election-year resource rules and advisory committee reforms.
overview: The committee recommended a Rental Renovation Licensing By-law that would require landlords to hold a licence when a tenant must move out for renovations after an N13 notice. It also recommended the fees and two new staff positions to run it {{vote:m6}}. A proposal to add landlord-paid rent top-ups, temporary housing and moving costs was deferred to the April 13, 2026 Council meeting {{vote:m8}}. Because this is a committee recommendation, Council still has to adopt it.

Earlier, staff reported that provincial changes to development charges and the regional water capacity limits are cutting the city's growth-related revenue. The committee recommended extending the Development Charges By-law by up to five years, keeping current rates while the forecast is uncertain. It also recommended moving $19,058,000 of development charges debt to the Cowan Recreation Centre gymnasium.

The committee also recommended Tier 2 community grants of $264,012, 2026 budgets for the Downtown and Belmont BIAs, and updated affordable rental housing fee waivers. It recommended a new election-year policy on use of city resources, revised advisory committee terms of reference, and continued work to speed up commercial business approvals.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended approving the by-law, its fees and two full-time staff positions to administer, inspect and enforce it {{vote:m6}}.
The committee recommended deferring the proposed landlord compensation and moving-cost provisions to the April 13, 2026 Council meeting {{vote:m8}}.
The committee recommended amending By-law 2022-071 to extend its term by up to five years.

The committee recommended reallocating $19,058,000 of development charges debt from the Upper Hidden Valley sewage pumping station to the Cowan Recreation Centre gymnasium, with matching reserve fund transfers.
The committee recommended amending the policy so more not-for-profit affordable housing projects qualify for waived development application and building permit fees.
The committee recommended approving $264,012 in 2026 Tier 2 community grants.
The committee recommended approving a policy limiting use of corporate resources for campaigning and amending the Council expense policy.
The committee recommended updating advisory committee terms and related policies, and directed staff to report in 2027 on modernizing the advisory committee model.

debate: On development charges, staff said legislated exemptions, discounts and deferrals, plus the water capacity limits, have left collections well below forecast, and that the reserve fund could go deeply negative without mitigation. Several councillors pressed on provincial funding and were told the province has signalled municipalities will not be made whole.

Some councillors questioned whether the shortfall would reach the tax base, and one raised extending the by-law while keeping flexibility for an earlier review. Staff said a rate change would need a full background study, and the extension gives certainty without blocking later changes in response to new federal and provincial announcements.

Supporters of the rental renovation by-law, including tenants and housing advocates, described stress, rent increases and long Landlord and Tenant Board delays. Many urged the committee to add rent top-ups and moving costs, as Hamilton, Toronto and Waterloo have done.

Landlords and other opponents argued the by-law duplicates provincial rules, adds cost and paperwork for responsible owners, and is outside municipal jurisdiction. Staff said the licensing model avoids overlapping provincial processes, and adding compensation could expose the by-law to legal challenge.

Some councillors worried about spending outside the budget process while the city faces development charge pressures, and asked to defer the staff-proposed staffing to budget. Others said the matter was urgent, and the mayor asked to separate the compensation amendment so it could get fuller consideration at Council.
